{{Short description|British Mathematician}}
'''Derek John Scott Robinson''' (born 25 September 1938 in [[Montrose, Scotland]])<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is a British mathematician, specialising in [[group theory]] and [[homological algebra]].<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Derek J. S. Robinson {{!}} Department of Mathematics|website=University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|url=https://math.illinois.edu/directory/profile/dsrobins}}(with comprehensive publication list)</ref>

==Education and career==
Robinson graduated in 1960 with a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Edinburgh]] and in 1963 with a Ph.D. from the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=homepage/> His Ph.D. thesis ''Theory of Subnormal Subgroups'' was supervised by [[Philip Hall]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=27098|name=Derek John Scott Robinson}}</ref> As a postdoc, Robinson was from 1963 to 1965 an instructor at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]. From 1965 to 1968 he was a [[lecturer]] at [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College (now named Queen Mary University of London)]]. At the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign he was an assistant professor from 1968 to 1969, an associate professor from 1969 to 1974, and a full professor from 1974 to 2007, when he retired as professor emeritus. He held visiting appointments in Switzerland, Italy, Germany, and Singapore.<ref name=homepage/>

Robinson's 1964 paper on [[T-group (mathematics)|T-group]]s<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Robinson | first1=Derek J. S. |title=Groups in which normality is a transitive relation|journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]|volume=10|issue=1|pages=21–38|year=1964|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-proceedings-of-the-cambridge-philosophical-society/article/abs/groups-in-which-normality-is-a-transitive-relation/E1EECC9F60124437962FBF9FDD8E81BA|doi=10.1017/S0305004100037403|bibcode=1964PCPS...60...21R |s2cid=119707269 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> has over 250 citations. He was awarded in 1970 the [[Sir Edmund Whittaker Memorial Prize]] and received in 1979 a [[Humboldt Prize]].<ref name=homepage/>
